newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber futures end up in line with Japan.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber futures end up in line with Japan.

text.p: Rubber futures closed slightly higher on Monday on the back of firmer Japanese prices in largely quiet trade, dealers said.
"Prices went up mainly because it followed Japanese prices. Otherwise, the market was very quiet and it may continue this way for the next few days," a local rubber trader said.
"It's really a dead market. I was trying to buy some rubber, but I couldn't find a seller. Most overseas buyers are still on the sidelines," another trader said.
Prices of Tokyo's benchmark April contract settled 1.3 yen up to 142.9.
Kobe's April contract settled at 142.8 yen from 141.5.
Dealers said news of sharply lower rubber stocks in Japan may provide some encouragement to the market although demand in the local exchange remains soft.
At around 0945 GMT, December RSS3 was seen at 126.00-127.00 U.S. cents a kg from 126.00 cents.
January RSS1 was seen at 184.00-186.00 Singapore cents (US$1.31-$1.33) a kg from the previous 183.75 cents.
January TSR20 was seen at 177.50-179.50 Singapore cents (US$1.27-$1.28) a kg from 177.50 cents.
